No path exists under strict safety within budget. Checking whether relaxing the "chase-entry" rule (entering a node the enemy vacates this tick) opens routes.**Briefing**: Two breakthroughs. First, the budget varies per level: Level 5 drains 1.6px/move = 40 moves, so the 27-move path is affordable. Second, my time-expanded BFS (simulating all four patrollers with strict no-collision/no-swap rules) found and verified a route: parity analysis proves the goal column and westward approaches are permanently blocked by the twin walkers, so the path loops south — down col 9, across to col 15, along row 44, up col 33, entering the goal from the east at a tick when both the row sweeper and column walkers are clear.

Action 187 | Level 8 | Attempt 1 | Plan Step 1/2 | Score: 7


[PLAN]
Adversarial pursuit is provably unwinnable — but deterministic tie-break models yield a 12-move win for some direction priorities. I need to identify the maroon's actual tie-break rule safely.**Briefing:** The maroon is a persistent equal-speed chaser (stepped (32,38)→(32,32) tracking me) and is effectively unkillable while chasing — any adjacency lets it step onto my node first. Adversarial pursuit analysis proves no guaranteed win exists, but the maroon must step toward me every move and appears deterministic: simulations show 6 of 24 tie-break priority orders are beatable via the cycle dodge, and its actual rule is still unobserved because every step so far was forced. My next two moves — down to (44,26), left to (44,20) — are the shared prefix of ALL winning routes and force the maroon into its first genuine tie, revealing its rule at zero cost. Budget: 21 moves left, winning line needs ~12.
